name: The Mountain God Rises (iQPS Launch 10)
agency: Institute for Q-shu Pioneers of Space
location_str: Rocket Lab LC-1A @ Rocket Lab Launch Complex 1, NZL
destination_explanation: Most of the satellites working today are down here, which has made this by far the most crowded stretch of space around the planet.
slot_a_text: Synthetic aperture radar Earth observation satellite for Japanese Earth imaging company iQPS.
slot_b_text: Low Earth orbit is anywhere from about 160 to 2,000 km up, where a satellite laps the planet roughly every 90 minutes. Everything there is falling; it just keeps missing the ground.

lg_slot_b_text: That was Rocket Lab's 21st launch of the year, 100th all time. Their year has run at a launch every couple of weeks. No Electron has failed in 59 flights.
lg_slot_c_text: Launch pad water deluge systems reduce the intense acoustic and pressure waves produced at liftoff, protecting the rocket and launch pad.
